verified_facts.fact: The blog post carries no author byline (unlike other blog.google posts such as the Pause Point one, which names an author). It is published under Google, not a named person.

The blog post body is FIVE

elements inside one rich-text block: an opening line ('Our September Pixel Drop is officially here, complete with handy new features and updates.'), one on Pixel VIPs plus the Gboard/Scam Detection line, one on Pixel Watch, one on Harry Potter, and the pointer 'Visit our community forum post to learn more.', which links to support.google.com/pixelphone/thread/466181739 -- i.e. Google itself designates that forum thread as its own detailed release note ('our community forum post'). verified_facts.fact: Blog wording for the phone features: 'Stay connected to your VIPs with updated home screen widgets that let you call or text people with a single tap, or switch between contacts using the bottom floating overlay navigation menu. New notification badges ensure you never miss a message. And Pixel now makes it easier to avoid scams with inline Gboard warnings in the U.S. and expanded Scam Detection for chat app notifications in more regions.

verified_facts.verbatim_quote: If you have a Pixel Watch, you’ll receive Raise to Talk improvements, and additional One Handed gesture app integrations, along with other bug fixes.

verified_facts.fact: Blog wording for the Harry Potter tie-in: 'Instantly customize your Pixel with Harry Potter Audiobook Packs to celebrate the release of Harry Potter: The Full-Cast Audio Editions on Audible. verified_facts.verbatim_quote: To begin your journey to Hogwarts, all eligible Pixel users will receive a two-month Audible free trial.

verified_facts.fact: The string 'Android Drop' occurs zero times on the blog post page. The related-stories rail lists exactly four items, none of them a 'September Android Drop' post; a probe URL for one returns 404. Corrected 2026-09-17 per corrections-tech.md must_fix 1: the prior record's claim that the rail 'shows a separate September Android Drop post' is deleted outright, re-confirmed absent on today's refetch.

Google's forum release note is titled 'September 2026 Pixel Drop' and defines a Pixel Drop as: 'Your Pixel devices become even more helpful with Pixel Drops. They're automatic software updates that send new and upgraded features to your phone.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Your Pixel devices become even more helpful with Pixel Drops. They’re automatic software updates that send new and upgraded features to your phone.

verified_facts.fact: Rollout timing, verbatim: 'Supported Pixel devices will receive these software updates starting today. The rollout of these features will continue over the coming weeks in phases, depending on carrier and device.' Google gives no completion date and names no carriers.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Supported Pixel devices will receive these software updates starting today. The rollout of these features will continue over the coming weeks in phases, depending on carrier and device.

verified_facts.fact: Google tells users they will be notified when the update is available and points them to 'Update to the latest Android version' (href support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/7680439) and 'update your apps' (href support.google.com/googleplay/answer/113412) -- i.e. some of these features arrive via app updates, not only the system update. The two hrefs, confirmed again 2026-09-17, replace an earlier inference with Google's own link targets.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: You will receive a notification once the system update is available for your device.

verified_facts.fact: The forum note's prose, under the heading 'Here are just some of the features to look forward to in the September Pixel Drop:', names exactly FOUR feature headings: 'Pixel VIPs updates', 'Harry Potter Audiobook Packs', 'Scam Detection comes to your keyboard and expands to new regions', and 'Pause Point expands to more Pixel devices'. Corrected 2026-09-17 per corrections-tech.md must_fix 5: the prior record wrote 'five named features'; five is the ROW count of the separate device-availability image (Scam Detection is split there into a keyboard row and a notification row), not the number of feature headings in the prose. The article must not write 'Google 列出五項功能'; it must say the prose names four headings and the matrix has five rows because Scam Detection is split in two there.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Here are just some of the features to look forward to in the September Pixel Drop:

verified_facts.fact: Feature 1, Pixel VIPs updates, verbatim: 'Stay seamlessly connected to your VIP contacts. With newly designed, expanded widget options, you can use quick actions to send a call or text to your VIP contacts with a single tap straight from your home screen. New, glanceable notification badges ensure you never miss an urgent or unread message, and you can also switch effortlessly between VIPs using the bottom floating menu.' No region, language or carrier condition is attached to this feature anywhere in the note, only the blanket footnote 5 (see below).
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With newly designed, expanded widget options, you can use quick actions to send a call or text to your VIP contacts with a single tap straight from your home screen.

verified_facts.fact: Feature 2, Harry Potter Audiobook Packs, verbatim: 'One tap changes your wallpaper, icons, and sounds with elements from the audiobooks - no wand required.' It is a theme pack (wallpaper + icons + sounds), tied to the release of 'Harry Potter: The Full-Cast Audio Editions' on Audible.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: One tap changes your wallpaper, icons, and sounds with elements from the audiobooks - no wand required.

verified_facts.fact: Feature 3a, Scam Detection in the keyboard: 'Starting in the U.S. on Pixel 6 and newer phones, Scam Detection is arriving directly on your Gboard (3) across your favorite messaging apps. When you start typing a response to a suspicious message, a "Likely scam" warning chip will appear right above your keys. Processing happens in real-time and on your device, keeping your conversations private to you (4).' Two conditions are stated in one sentence: United States only, AND Pixel 6 or newer; note the conditions are 'Starting in the U.S.', not 'only in the U.S.'. Corrected 2026-09-18 in the second factcheck round: the page's own text carries footnote markers inside these sentences -- '(3)' sits between 'Gboard' and 'across', '(4)' between 'private to you' and the full stop -- so the sentence as previously stored was NOT a contiguous string on the page. verbatim_quote below is trimmed to the part that is contiguous and that carries both conditions.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Starting in the U.S. on Pixel 6 and newer phones, Scam Detection is arriving directly on your Gboard

verified_facts.fact: The on-device / real-time processing claim for keyboard Scam Detection is Google's own statement, not something this site tested: 'Processing happens in real-time and on your device, keeping your conversations private to you'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Processing happens in real-time and on your device, keeping your conversations private to you

verified_facts.fact: Footnote 3, attached to the word 'Gboard', says the keyboard warning is not Gboard-exclusive: 'Available on other keyboards with Keyboard Suggestions.' Not used in the article body (kept for completeness); the article states the Gboard/US/Pixel-6+ facts only.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Available on other keyboards with Keyboard Suggestions.

verified_facts.fact: Footnote 4, attached to the keyboard Scam Detection paragraph, narrows it further: 'Available only in select languages in the US.' Google does not name which languages.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Available only in select languages in the US.

verified_facts.fact: Feature 3b, Scam Detection in chat notifications, verbatim: 'Already available in the US for Pixel 6+ devices, we're now expanding this feature to nine new countries (Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, Singapore, and the United Kingdom) and six new languages (Arabic, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese, and Spanish), helping protect even more people worldwide.' That is exactly nine countries and six languages, listed by name. Taiwan is not among them.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: we’re now expanding this feature to nine new countries (Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, Singapore, and the United Kingdom) and six new languages (Arabic, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese, and Spanish)

verified_facts.fact: Google describes the notification-level Scam Detection as pre-existing, not new in this Drop, and links to Google's own November 2025 Pixel Drop post. Row count re-verified 2026-09-18 by grid-line detection on the PNG: 7 horizontal rules, i.e. a header band plus 5 feature bands. verbatim_quote is deliberately empty: these row labels are pixels inside thread-466181739-2189480914184742135.png and appear nowhere in the thread's text, so no string search of the page can reproduce them -- they are the editor's reading of the image.

editorial_brief:
READER: a Taiwanese Pixel owner -- Pixel 6 through Pixel 11, possibly a Pixel Watch -- who saw a headline about scam warnings and wants to know whether anything in it reaches their phone.

ANGLE: a Feature Drop is not one thing. Its features are gated three different ways, stated in three different places. (a) Device gate: the matrix ticks 24 phone models, Pixel 6/6a up to Pixel 11 Pro Fold, for all five rows, and ticks Pixel Tablet for none. (b) Region/language gate: keyboard Scam Detection is US-only and 'select languages in the US'; notification Scam Detection adds nine named countries and six named languages this Drop, on top of an eleven-region/eight-language cumulative state the Help Centre states separately and without a date; the Audible trial covers ten named countries until 14 January 2027, and the theme packs themselves expire 31 December 2026 with no country limit of their own. (c) Pairing gate: the watch's Proactive suggestions need a Pixel Watch 5 paired with a Pixel 11 with Gemini and proactive assistance turned on. Taiwan appears in none of the lists. Say that plainly and let the reader check their own model; do not turn it into a complaint about Google or a prediction of when Taiwan gets it.

SECOND ANGLE: where the real release note lives. The blog post says 'If you have a Pixel Watch' -- the linked note says Pixel Watch 5 only. The blog names three phone-side items in prose -- the linked forum note names four feature headings and a five-row device matrix, including Pause Point, which the blog never mentions. The blog gives no dates -- the note gives two. And the device matrix that answers 'does my phone get this' is a PNG screenshot inside a forum thread with no text alternative. A concrete point about how to read a vendor Feature Drop, grounded in having actually opened both pages.

THIRD ANGLE, small but genuinely useful for a Taiwan reader: Circle to Search and Google Lens, on the same Help Centre page as the region-gated Scam Detection feature, carry no region or language restriction at all -- a different (AI/web-lookup) mechanism, not to be blurred with on-device Scam Detection, but worth naming because it is the one scam-checking route not fenced behind the eleven-region list.

STRUCTURE: 9/15 announcement and where the real note lives; phone features and the device matrix (table closes this section); region/language detail including the Help Centre's cumulative snapshot and Circle to Search (diagram closes this section); the Pixel Watch 5 side and its pairing condition; what is not stated, including Taiwan, dates, build numbers and the Pixel Tablet row.

LIVED-EXPERIENCE material stays out or is explicitly editor-labelled per BRIEF.md; none was needed given how much first-party detail exists.
must_not_write: No buying or upgrade advice of any kind -- tech.md bars 該不該買 / 值不值得升級 / 哪一支比較好. Listing which model gets which feature is allowed; concluding which model to get is not.
Do not write that Taiwan is excluded, blocked or unsupported. Google names Taiwan nowhere. Write 官方公告未提及台灣 and, for the features with no region list, 官方只說可用性可能因國家或語言而異.

Do not restate Google's capability claims as fact. 'Most accurate GPS route tracking', 'low latency', 'real-time', 'processing happens on your device', 'keeping your conversations private' are all Google 表示. This site ran no test -- never write 我們實測.

Do not invent an Android version, a phone build number, a September 2026 Pixel Watch security patch level, a Taiwan launch date or a rollout completion date. None exists in any source; the only build published is the watch's CP3A.260905.002.
Do not silently fix Google's duplicated 'DE' in the image's language list (AR, DE, ES, FR, DE, PT, and JA). Use the six-language prose list for the body.
Do not merge the ten Audible countries with the nine Scam Detection countries -- they are different sets (Audible adds Italy and Spain, omits Mexico and Singapore).
Do not carry the blog's loose phrasing 'If you have a Pixel Watch' without Google's own restriction to Pixel Watch 5.
Do not attribute anything to the forum posters' personal names ('Kush M.', 'Stefanie Frederick'). Attribute to Google.
Do not describe or evaluate Pixel 11 / Pixel Watch 5 hardware. The sources only use those names.
No finance disclaimer callout -- tech.md says the tech vertical must not carry one.
No trademark, wordmark, logo, mascot or UI screenshot in the hero or the SVG diagram; write product names as plain text.
Do not write anything about how scams are actually carried out. Batch 3's threat-report rule applies: scope and what the user should do, never attack technique.
No list formatting, no Markdown, no emoji, no Simplified Chinese characters in the zh-TW pack.

Do not write 'Google 列出五項功能' -- the forum note's prose names four feature headings; five is the device-matrix's row count because Scam Detection is split into a keyboard row and a notification row there. State both numbers with what each one counts.

Do not write that the Pixel Watch 5 / Wear OS 7 update 'was announced on 15 September'. Revised 2026-09-18: the watch thread DOES display a date to readers (rendered client-side) -- 'Sep 2, 2026' in a UTC+8 browser -- so 'the note carries no visible date' is false and must not be written either. Print the displayed date only with the caveat that the browser converts it into the reader's own timezone, and never print the raw 2026-09-01T19:47:42Z instant as the note's date.

Revised in the second round, 2026-09-18: do not write that the watch note 「早於部落格文章」 or that it was published two weeks before the Pixel Drop. What the page gives is the THREAD's date (1788292062825882 = 2026-09-01T19:47:42Z, 2026-09-02 in Taipei), and the note's own build string CP3A.260905.002 carries a later stamp than that date, so the content a reader sees today was edited after the thread was created. The article therefore states only what the page shows and how it is produced, and takes its event date from the blog post's printed 'Sep 15, 2026'. Do not turn the two dates into a chronology.

Do not describe the phone forum note as '2026 年 9 月 15 日發布的論壇公告'. The thread displays only a relative label ('2 days ago', 'Last edited 2 days ago'); no absolute publication date for that thread is printed anywhere a reader can see. Only the blog post carries a printed dateline, 'Sep 15, 2026'.
Do not put a date on 'First introduced on Pixel 11' for Pause Point. The forum note gives none ('May' occurs zero times in it), and the Pause Point blog post it links to is not in sources[].

Do not import the Pixel Watch security bulletin's state (source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/pixel-watch) into the article. It is not in sources[], it is live data, and the claim would be a negative one ('no September bulletin yet'). The article may only repeat that the note points readers there.

Do not write that Google published no Traditional-Chinese version of the Pixel Drop blog post. That rested on probing a derived intl/zh-tw URL, which BRIEF.md counts as guessing. The article now says only that the blog post and the two forum notes it cites are English, and that the Help Centre page has a Chinese version carrying Google's own machine-translation warning.

Do not describe the sign-off 'Thanks, Google Pixel Watch Support Team' as being at the end of the watch note -- it sits near the top, right after the security-bulletin line; the note's last section is 'Previous Pixel Watch Updates'.
Do not write 'Offline Gemini gives four examples' -- Google names three (timer, workout start/stop, do-not-disturb) plus an open-ended 'other device actions', which is not a fourth named example.

Do not present the Help Centre's 11-region/8-language list as complete eligibility criteria on its own -- it states no Pixel model requirement, while the forum note and device matrix require Pixel 6 or newer.

Do not conflate Circle to Search / Google Lens (AI and web-lookup based, no stated region limit) with the on-device Scam Detection feature this Drop expands, and do not invent an official Traditional-Chinese product name for Circle to Search -- none was found in any source; keep the English product names as plain text.

Do not conflate call-level Scam Detection or the Google Messages spam folder (both documented on the same Help Centre page) with the chat-notification and keyboard Scam Detection variants this Drop actually changes.
